states.name: light
states.gap: Tighter and greyer page. The line pitch is about 74 device px against about 76 in B (roughly 2.7% less leading), the paper is #F7F7F7 against B's #F9F9F9, and glyphs advance about 1.5% wider (the same first line runs 1620 px against 1596), so A's lines are slightly denser and its paper a little dimmer.
states.gapTheirs: B's heading markers sit inside the text column instead of hanging in the margin. '#' starts at the body's left edge (about 622 px), so 'The Lighthouse' starts about 50 px to the right of the body text and 'What the sea keeps' about 75 px to the right. A hangs '#' and '##' to the left of the column, so both headings start exactly on the body's left edge.
states.verdict: B spaces its lines a little more loosely on slightly whiter paper, but every heading breaks the left edge of the column, and each '#' level pushes the title further right. A writer scanning down the page sees that stagger at every section. A holds one straight left edge from heading to body, so the text reads as a single block with the margin framing it. A is a shade denser and greyer, but that costs less than a broken column edge.
secondary: Both images are 2880x1800.
The measure is essentially the same: the text column runs from about 622 to 2243 device px in both, roughly 62–64 characters per line.
B's slightly narrower glyphs pull 'she' back onto the first line of the second paragraph, so A and B break that paragraph's lines differently.
A's list item '- the rope…' sits about 34 px above the status bar's rule, which crowds the bottom edge. In B, the last visible body line has more clearance.
The left and right margins are about 622 px and 637 px in both, so the text column is centred in the window in both.
Excluded by the brief: page top (B opens lower), marker colour (B's are grey) and the caret's ends.

states.name: short
states.gap: The measure is a little tighter and the lines sit a little closer. Glyph advance is ≈26.8 vs 26.4 device px per character (1134 vs 1118 display px over the same 61-character line), so a paragraph line wraps one word sooner ('empty,' / 'and'). Line pitch is ≈74 vs 76 device px, which makes the paragraphs look slightly more packed.
states.gapTheirs: The heading marker isn't hung in the margin. '# ' starts at x≈622 device px, on the same edge as the body text, so the heading words start about 51 px to the right of the body's left edge (≈673 vs 622). The text column's left edge breaks at every heading, and the left margin reads as 622 px for the body but 673 px for heading words.
states.verdict: Both pages use the same near-white paper and a centred column of about 1630 px with roughly 625 px of margin on each side. The real difference is the left edge. B hangs the '#' out in the margin, so heading and body share one straight edge at x=622. A pushes the heading words in by a marker's width, so the column's left edge jogs at every heading, and you notice it every time your eye goes back to the start of a line. B pays for that with slightly tighter lines and a wider advance that wraps a word early, but a crooked left edge is harder to ignore than 2 px of leading.
